description.narrative:
The innovation project addresses the systemic gaps in GBV prevention, response, and child protection in Southwest State, Somalia, where protracted conflict, displacement, and weak institutional capacity have left women and children acutely vulnerable. Indisplacement sites, GBV survivors face high risks of sexual violence, exploitation, and stigma, yet traditional protection mechanisms remain fragmented, paper-based, and resource-constrained, resulting in delayed referrals, breaches of confidentiality, and inconsistent survivor-centred care. Child protection services are equally overstretched, with limited access to safe, trauma-informed spaces for displaced children, leaving them exposed to psychosocial distress, neglect, and harmful coping strategies.
At a structural level, the humanitarian funding system compounds these gaps. Most resources are channelled through international organizations, with local actors relegated to sub-grantee roles. This undermines local ownership, sustainability, and accountability, despite local NGOs having the trust and proximity required to deliver sensitive protection services effectively. Donor concerns over fiduciary risk further limit direct investment in national actors, constraining innovation and responsiveness. The project responds to these dual challenges byintroducing digital innovations—such as offline-capable GBVIMS+/Primero case management, mobile referral pathways, gamified trauma-healing tools, and digital dashboards—and embedding them within a locally led governance and funding model. This model, led by PASOSwith World Vision Somalia in an advisory role, directly tests whether Somali NGOs can manage significant donor funds responsibly while delivering high-quality, tech-enabled protection services.
In doing so, the project tackles both the immediate protection crisis facing survivors and children, and the structural funding imbalance that prevents local actors from scaling effective, context-driven solutions.
PASOS solution is a locally led, technology-enabled protection model that simultaneously addresses service delivery gaps and structural funding challenges in Southwest State. Unlike conventional models where international actors control funds and local NGOs deliver services with limited autonomy, this pilot places PASOS in the lead—managing direct funds, governing through a Consortium Coordination Unit (CCU), and operationalizing ERP-based systems for transparency. World Vision Somalia provides advisory andtechnical support, ensuring compliance and safeguarding without undermining local ownership.
On the programmatic side, the solution introduces digital innovations rarely integrated in Somalia’s protection response: • Offline-capable GBVIMS+/Primero for secure case management, enablingtimely, confidential survivor support in low-connectivity contexts. • Integrated mobile referral pathways andalerts to reduce delays in service provision. • Child-Friendly Spaces, equipped with solar-powered digital learning, gamified trauma-healing apps, and adaptive technologies for children with disabilities. • Community-managed dashboards and SMS feedback loops, embedding accountability to affected populations in real time. This differs from ongoing approaches by combining direct funding with digital accountability, creating a dual innovation: empowering national actors structurally while modernizing protection systems technically. Assumptions:  Donors will trust ERP-based financial and compliance tools as sufficient safeguards for direct funding.  Communities will accept digital tools if paired with sensitization and participatory design.  International partners can shift into advisory roles without disrupting quality.
The project will be implemented through a locally led consortium,with PASOS as the lead organization and World Vision Somalia providing technical and compliance support. Oversight will be managed by a Consortium Coordination Unit (CCU), co-chaired by PASOS and World Vision, ensuring transparent governance, financial accountability, and joint learning.
The project will be implemented through a locally led consortium, with PASOS as the lead organization and World Vision Somalia providing technical and compliance support. Oversight will be managed by a Consortium Coordination Unit (CCU), co-chaired by PASOS and World Vision, ensuring transparent governance, financial accountability, and joint learning. Major activities will include: 1. Operationalizing the Direct Funding <(>&<)> Governance Model PASOS will establish and lead the CCU, manage funds through an ERP-based financial system, and coordinate independent audits. World Vision will provide technical mentoring on compliance and safeguarding without assuming control. Monthly CCU meetings will guide decision-making andmonitor risk. 2. Digital GBV Response PASOS will deploy GBVIMS+/Primero in three protection centres (Baidoa, Hudur, and Diinsoor). Twenty caseworkers (including women and youth) will be trainedon digital literacy, survivor-centred case management, andethical data protection. Integrated referral pathways will link legal, psychosocial, and health services, supported by mobile alerts for rapid follow-up. 3. Child-Friendly Spaces (CFS) Three safe spaces will be established or upgraded with solar-powered learning stations, gamified trauma-healing apps, and adaptive technologies for children with disabilities. Facilitators and volunteers will be trained in trauma-informed care and disability inclusion. Structured psychosocial activities will support 500+children, overseen by community protection committees. 4. Community Engagement <(>&<)> Accountability Community dashboards and SMS feedback systems will capture real-time input from survivors and families. Quarterly governanceand learning reviews will document progress and share lessons with DRA stakeholders. This implementation approach ensures local ownership, community accountability, and evidence generation, while delivering lifesaving protection services. 5. Capacity Building andCoordination Assistthe Protection Cluster in delivering GBVIMS+/Primero induction training programs for newly recruited staff. Provide targeted support to the Ministry of Women in coordinating gender-based violence and protection initiatives, ensuring stronger alignment with national frameworks and cluster mechanisms.

participating-org.narrative:
Peace Action Society Organization for Somalia (PASOS) is a professionally managed and committed national Non-Governmental and Non-profit-making organization, founded by civil society groups on 1st January 1997 in Mogadishu, Somalia.
The primary focus of PASOS ison the problems of the poor in their struggle to obtain a life of justice <(>&<)> dignity, environment stabilization, food security<(>&<)> livelihood, getting access to clean portable water and health services, empowerment of the community for self-governance are the most important components of its mission. Gender justice, advocacy on human rights, democracy, peace and conflict resolution in society child protection and child rights, natural resource management, and livelihood security are our primary areas of concern as well
PASOS vision is for a self-sufficient and sustainable Somalia.PASOS mission is to empower the vulnerable and the underprivileged communities in Somalia in order to bring about sustainable development and positive social transformation while focusing on equity, justice and human rights.
PASOS’ goal is to: 1. Improve the quality of life for the vulnerable, disadvantaged, and marginalized communities. 2. Enhance emergency response and livelihood crisis intervention 3. Increase access to safe portable water, sanitation and good hygiene conditions. 4. Increase access to quality education 5. Promote sustainable use of environmental resources 6. Enhance human rights awareness, democracy and good governance 7. Promote child protection and child rights
PASOS works in all federal states of Somalia particularly the districts indicated below • Benadir region: all 18 districts • Galgadud Region: Dusamareb, Gura-el, Adado, Abudwak and Balanbale districts • Gedo Region: Elwak and Bardera districts • Jubba Region: Kismayo • Lower Shabelle: Afgoa,Awdhegle, Elasha and Walaweyn • Bay Region: Baidoa, Burhakaba, Dinsor, Bardale and Qansahdhere
PASOS is a member of various collaborating organizations including Somali Support Secretariat (SSS), UN cluster member of Agriculture/Livelihoods, Health, Nutrition, Protection <(>&<)> WASH sectors, member of Food Security (FSEDSC), Agricultural working group, Gender Based Violence, HIV/AIDS, Gender, Human Rights, Somali Human Rights DefendersNetwork (SOHRIDEN), Consortium for Southern Somalia NGOs (COSSONGOS) and Child Protection Network in Banadir (CPN). PASOS also is member of South-Central Aids Commission (SCAC), Coalition for Peace in Africa (COPA). PASOS is registered under the Ministry of Interior Affairs of the Federal Government, Ministry of Agriculture and regional federal government Administrations such as Southwest state, Jubba-land state, Puntland State, Hir-shabelle state and Galmudug state
